narration: That button promised 'cancel anytime.' When you tried, it was seven screens, a chat bot, and a guilt trip. Here's what that deliberate design is actually costing you.
visual: Smartphone drops in from above showing a friendly green 'CANCEL ANYTIME' badge, then an animated chain of 7 labeled steps — ACCOUNT, REASONS?, DISCOUNT?, SURVEY, ARE YOU SURE?, CALL US, GIVE UP — builds down the screen, ending with a red 'BY DESIGN' badge

narration: Companies pay UX designers specifically to make cancellation hard. It's called a dark pattern. In 2023 the FTC documented $1.2 billion in consumer harm from this one trick.
visual: Light background with a flowchart: 'CANCEL ANYTIME' (green) -> 'WHY LEAVING?' -> 'WANT A DISCOUNT?' -> 'GIVE UP. PAY AGAIN.' (red), then a red FTC stamp crashes in showing '$1.2B IN CONSUMER HARM'

narration: A hard-cancel design keeps 15% more paying users who wanted to leave. That's not a bug — it's the whole business model. They're literally counting on you giving up.
visual: Dark background: grid of 20 person silhouettes animates in row by row — 17 gray, 3 highlighted red with padlock icons — then '15%' in big red text with 'STAY TRAPPED' subtitle

narration: The average person has four subscriptions they completely forgot about. At $25 a month each, that's $100 every month — $1,200 a year draining out of your account silently.
visual: 4 subscription cards (STREAMING, FITNESS APP, CLOUD STORAGE, NEWS SERVICE) each showing '$25/mo' slide in from left one by one, then a counter climbs from $0 to $1,200 labeled 'DRAINED PER YEAR'

narration: Most people spend 15 minutes trying to cancel a single subscription — and 40% give up before finishing. That quit attempt you abandoned? Another $25 charge lands next month.
visual: Dark background: analog clock face with minute hand sweeping to 15 minutes past, confused person silhouette facing a looping loading circle on a phone screen, then a red '40% GIVE UP MID-CANCEL' badge springs in

narration: Open your bank statement and find every subscription charge. Cancel the ones you haven't used this month before the next billing date. That's $1,200 a year back in your pocket.
visual: Light background: 4 bank statement rows slide in from right showing subscription charges, each gets a green checkmark one by one as it's cancelled, then a red '$1,200 BACK IN YOUR POCKET' badge springs in with 'FOLLOW FOR MORE MONEY TRAPS' CTA
